items.t: Tencent stock: U.S. weighs curbs on remote AI chip access
sum: В четверг, 12 ноября 2026 года, Yahoo Finance сообщила, что Министерство торговли США готовит правила, которые могут запретить китайским компаниям, занимающимся искусственным интеллектом, удаленный доступ к передовым чипам через центры обработки данных за пределами Китая. Tencent была среди компаний, упомянутых в отчете, имеющих соглашения о размещении центров обработки данных за рубежом.

Предлагаемая мера может распространить существующий контроль над полупроводниками еще на семь стран, включая Малайзию, Сингапур и Таиланд. Сообщаемая политика все еще находится в стадии подготовки и не была окончательно доработана, поэтому ее окончательные масштабы и сроки остаются открытыми.

Удаленный доступ к передовым процессорам дает китайским технологическим компаниям возможность использовать вычислительные мощности, имеющиеся за границей, без импорта оборудования напрямую в Китай. Ужесточение контроля может усложнить планирование инфраструктуры искусственного интеллекта Tencent и повысить важность отечественных альтернатив.

Для инвесторов главный вопрос заключается в том, останутся ли политические дебаты главным риском или станут практическим ограничением вычислительных мощностей. Эта проблема добавляет нормативный аспект усилиям компании по расширению услуг искусственного интеллекта во всей ее продуктовой экосистеме.

sum: Tencent Holdings is showing early commercial benefits from artificial intelligence in advertising and cloud services, but the expansion is also raising the investment burden. A November 7 analysis published by PR.com said the company is increasingly embedding AI in businesses with established customers and revenue models.

Tencent reported second-quarter revenue of 204.8 billion yuan, up 11 percent year over year. Marketing Services revenue rose 22 percent to 43.6 billion yuan, with the company pointing to improvements in AI-driven advertising recommendations, its AIM+ campaign-management system and marketing tools across the Weixin ecosystem.

The analysis said Tencent's clearest AI-related gains are appearing inside advertising and cloud rather than in standalone consumer chatbot products. Cloud growth accelerated into the low-20 percent range year over year, supported by AI-related demand, international expansion and wider use of general cloud services. AI-related cloud revenue included GPU rental and model-as-a-service offerings.

That route gives Tencent a potential advantage: AI can improve existing customer relationships instead of relying solely on direct consumer payments for new applications. Better advertising recommendations can support campaign performance, while cloud services can monetize demand for computing capacity and model access.
The expansion remains expensive. Tencent's second-quarter capital expenditure reached 52.8 billion yuan, an increase of 176 percent from a year earlier, as the company expanded computing capacity.

Non-IFRS operating profit rose 9 percent to 75.6 billion yuan. The analysis also compared that result with an adjusted figure of 86.1 billion yuan excluding newer AI products including Hy, Yuanbao, CodeBuddy, WorkBuddy and Xiaowei. It cautioned that this comparison does not represent a separately reported loss for those products, but it indicates that the newer initiatives remain investment-heavy.

For investors, the central issue is not whether Tencent can demonstrate capable models, but whether usage in advertising, cloud and enterprise products can produce durable revenue and cash returns. Higher infrastructure and development costs may weigh on near-term profitability before monetization reaches scale.

sum: Hong Kong’s Hang Seng Index closed the week of 2–6 November 2026 at 24,481.86, up 5.10%, its best week since early March, as investors rotated out of AI hardware into discounted Chinese internet platforms and Beijing stepped up market support. China’s inflation and trade data and Singles’ Day headline next week.

The Hang Seng Index, the main benchmark of the Hong Kong Stock Exchange, ended Friday 6 November 2026 at 24,481.86, down 315.12 points or 1.27% on the day. For the week, it gained 1,187.44 points, or 5.10%, from the previous Friday’s close of 23,294.42, its largest weekly advance since the first week of March 2026.

The Hang Seng China Enterprises Index rose 5.24% over the week to 8,274.10, and the Hang Seng Tech Index surged about 8.6%. Even so, the benchmark remains well below its 52-week high of about 28,056, leaving room for further recovery.

Hong Kong rose for four straight sessions. The index gained 0.42% to 23,393.32 on Monday 2 November, led by Xiaomi, CATL, Alibaba and Tencent, then added 0.57% to 23,525.97 on Tuesday and 1.67% to 23,919.50 on Wednesday as global markets rallied after the US midterm elections.

Thursday 5 November was the standout. The Hang Seng soared 877.48 points, or 3.67%, to 24,796.98, its best day since February 2025, while the Hang Seng Tech Index jumped 5.55%, its biggest gain of the year. On Friday the global AI sell-off caught up with Hong Kong, and the index fell 1.27%, but it held on to most of the week’s gains.

The rally was a rotation. As investors sold AI hardware stocks in the US, Japan, Korea and Taiwan, they bought Chinese internet platforms that had become cheap: the Hang Seng Tech Index traded at around 13 times forward earnings in October, its lowest valuation since 2024. Thursday’s jump also triggered one of the biggest short squeezes in years.

Alibaba and Tencent each rose more than 7% on Thursday and Meituan close to 7%. Tencent had already gained almost 6% after launching its new Hunyuan AI model with visual understanding and computer-use capabilities, showing that investors still reward Chinese AI applications even as they sell hardware.

sum: Tencent has spent the past year in the headlines for AI, cloud expansion, and fresh regulatory twists, from Nvidia chip approvals that stalled in Beijing to a multibillion dollar Oracle chip leasing deal that never actually went ahead. Investors who held Tencent over the past year are down 32.4%, including dividends. The move put Tencent in the middle of this trade. Scan 53 AI infrastructure stocks for other companies exposed to it.
The shares cost HK$629 at the start of the period, and anyone looking at Tencent then had to choose which earnings story felt more realistic.

On the optimistic side, analysts argued the stock was worth about HK$687 as a fair value anchor, based on assumptions that revenue could compound at 10.5% with profit margins reaching 31.6% and a future P/E of 23.0x over three years.

The more cautious case put fair value nearer HK$508, with expectations of 12.0% annual revenue growth but profit margins capped at 24.0% and a future P/E of 22.0x over a longer five year horizon, while regulatory risk stayed front and center.

Tencent’s heavy AI push showed up clearly in the Q2 2026 numbers. Revenue moved to CNY 204.8b and net income edged to CNY 56.0b, yet the net margin slipped from 30.2% to 27.4%. That combination supported the cautious case that higher AI spending and chip constraints would weigh on profitability even as the top line held up.
The lesson is simple. When a story hinges on AI investment lifting future earnings, keep an eye on the net margin line and how it moves against any revenue increase, not just the headline growth.

items.t: Hong Kong Stocks Surge 877 Points to Breach 24,000 Mark; Turnover Hits HK$356.6 Billion, a Near Four-Month High
sum: Hong Kong stocks on the 5th bucked the trend seen in other major Asian markets. The Hang Seng Index closed sharply higher by 877 points, or 3.67%, at 24,796, reclaiming the 24,000-point threshold in one stroke. Full-day turnover reached HK$356.6 billion (approximately $45.5 billion), marking the largest single-day volume in nearly four months. On the same day, Japanese and Taiwanese stocks both fell more than 2%, making Hong Kong's contrarian strength the most conspicuous focus in the region.

Across the board, aside from artificial intelligence (AI)-related names, nearly all sectors advanced, with traditional tech platform stocks in online shopping, gaming, and retail posting particularly strong gains. Tencent Holdings (0700.HK) closed at HK$430 (approximately $55), up 7.17%; Alibaba (9988.HK) closed at HK$109 (approximately $14), up 8.44%; and Meituan (3690.HK) closed at HK$80.3 (approximately $10), up 6.78%. The Hang Seng Tech Index opened higher in the morning session at 3,992.39, up 56.37 points, or 1.43%.

The capital driving this rally came from multiple directions. Market participants noted that after the US midterm election results became clear, some funds withdrew from US AI stocks and rotated into Hong Kong equities. Stabilizing international geopolitical conditions and falling oil prices also eased market pressure. In addition, the People's Bank of China's stated support for measures such as share buybacks gave the market room to imagine capital inflows into Hong Kong stocks.

On the corporate front, Tencent's long-teased next-generation large language model, the official version of Hunyuan Hy4, was released on the 4th. The series' parameter scale rose from under 300B in Hy3 to 770B, with the next generation, Hy5, set to expand further. Hy4 also introduced visual understanding capabilities for the first time and supports computer operation. This development became an important catalyst for Tencent's share price. Other internet and tech stocks strengthened in tandem: Xiaomi rose more than 4%, while Meituan and NetEase gained more than 3%. Gold stocks opened higher, with Zijin Gold International up more than 7%. Innovative drug concept stocks extended their gains, with BeiGene up more than 2%.

sum: If you had bought Tencent Music Entertainment Group at the start of this review period expecting smartphone adoption, fan clubs and live shows to re-rate the business, the result has been brutal. Investors who held Tencent Music Entertainment Group over the past year are down 60.5%, including dividends. If that entry decision was based on analysts’ 2025 assumptions for double digit revenue growth, still high margins and a near 30x future P/E, what exactly did that thesis overlook?
The useful thing about a Narrative is that the reasoning is checkable: the assumptions sit beside the argument, and together they imply an estimated Fair Value you can disagree with.
The Argument You Would Have Been Weighing Up On Tencent Music Entertainment Group
The shares cost US$22.31 at the start of the period, and Tencent Music Entertainment Group sat between two very different stories about what came next.

On the upbeat side, one narrative put Fair Value at US$28.34. That view leaned on 14.8% assumed annual revenue growth, helped by rising smartphone usage, fan-focused features such as SVIP and "bubble," and a 29.8x future P/E assumption.

The more cautious script pointed to a Fair Value of US$14.54. This camp focused on tightening Chinese regulation, higher compliance costs, and fierce competition from platforms like NetEase Cloud Music and ByteDance as key risks to future performance.

The big swing factor was Tencent Music Entertainment Group closing the US$2.4b Himalaya acquisition and folding podcast revenue into Q2 2026, which helped lift total revenue to RMB 8,933m and supported the optimistic case on new formats and fan time spent. At the same time, net margin slipped from 28.5% to 27.7%, which challenged the easy high margin assumption.

sum: Tencent is scheduled to publish its third-quarter 2026 results on Wednesday, November 18. The company's investor relations page lists the release in its 2026 calendar, while Futu's Oct. 15 earnings preview provides the market context.

Futu reported that GF Securities expects Tencent's third-quarter revenue to reach RMB 209.8 billion, an increase of 9 percent from a year earlier. UBS expects revenue growth of 7 percent. The forecasts point to continued expansion, but they also frame the quarter around the cost of Tencent's artificial intelligence build-out.

Futu said UBS estimates AI-related operating expenses at RMB 16 billion for the quarter and adjusted operating profit at RMB 71 billion, down 2 percent year over year. GF Securities expects adjusted operating profit of RMB 70 billion, a 4 percent decline. The figures suggest that infrastructure depreciation and research spending could absorb part of the benefit from higher-margin activities.

Advertising is expected to remain a major growth driver, with the two research houses cited by Futu forecasting an 18 percent year-over-year increase. Domestic gaming revenue is forecast to grow by 12 to 13 percent, while overseas gaming revenue is expected to decline by 3 to 6 percent as Supercell faces a high comparison base and a limited new-title pipeline.

Futu also reported that UBS raised its Tencent target price by 3.9 percent to HKD 740, while GF Securities set a fair target price of HKD 644.54. These analyst estimates remain forward-looking and will be tested by the official results next week.

Tencent inks first deal for carbon-removal credits outside China
sum: [BEIJING] Tencent Holdings will buy 300,000 carbon removal credits from an agroforestry project in Indonesia, marking the first deal of its kind for the Chinese technology firm outside its domestic market.

Tencent has entered a 10-year agreement with Singapore-based carbon developer Thryve.Earth to purchase credits generated from a project on the island of Sulawesi, it said on Wednesday (Jul 8). Alphabet’s Google struck a separate 10-year offtake deal for 260,000 credits from the same project, while consulting firm McKinsey agreed to buy 75,000. The average price for agroforestry credits in Asia is currently around US$21.40, according to carbon data company Sylvera.

Carbon removal will play a key role in Tencent’s commitment to achieve carbon neutrality in its own operations and supply chain by 2030, a company spokesperson said by email. While reducing emissions remains the top priority, high-quality carbon credits can help address residual emissions and deliver climate impacts, the spokesperson said.

Agroforestry projects, which combine agriculture with removing carbon by planting or increasing forest cover, have the potential to deliver up to 310 million tons of carbon-dioxide removal annually and could play an important role in efforts to limit global warming. The willingness of corporate buyers to keep doing such deals offers a counterpoint to news earlier this year that Microsoft Corp was pulling back.

The Thryve.Earth project will restore degraded land in Sulawesi, an island in the centre of the Indonesian archipelago on which tropical rainforests have been destroyed by agriculture, soil erosion and invasive species. The idea is to develop a “mixed crop farming system” that sequesters carbon, replenishes soils, increases biodiversity and provides income for local farmers.

The project envisages an upper tree canopy of sugar palm plants and timber trees, a mid-layer of papayas, avocado, coffee, and bananas, and ground-level annual crops such as chilli and corn. The layers are intended to optimise land productivity and provide income streams that are “significantly more valuable than the carbon revenues alone, aligning carbon sequestration benefits with economic incentives,” Thryve.Earth said.

Reborn Coffee Celebrates Grand Opening of Shenzhen Flagship Location at Tencent Headquarters Campus, Marking Strategic Next Phase of China Expansion
sum: Opening Establishes a Foundation for Multi-Province Growth Across China and Reinforces Reborn Coffee's Broader International Expansion Strategy

BREA, Calif., March 24, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Reborn Coffee Inc. (Nasdaq: REBN) (the "Company"), a leader in the specialty coffee market, announced today the successful grand opening of its flagship location in Shenzhen, China on March 18, 2026. Located within Tencent's new headquarters campus, the opening marks a significant milestone in Reborn Coffee's international growth strategy and further advances the Company's previously announced expansion initiatives in China.

The Shenzhen flagship reflects the Company's broader strategy to build a scalable presence across multiple provinces in China. As one of China's leading centers of technology, innovation, and modern urban development, Shenzhen offers a strategically aligned entry point for the brand, with a consumer base that is highly responsive to premium, design-driven, and innovation-led lifestyle concepts.

The Company believes this opening represents an important starting point for Reborn Coffee's future growth in China. Beyond the launch of a single flagship store, the Shenzhen location is intended to serve as a foundation for broader regional expansion, brand visibility, and operational development in one of the world's most dynamic consumer markets. By delivering high-quality refreshment services in the heart of a major technology ecosystem, Reborn Coffee is positioning itself to participate meaningfully in technology-driven urban spaces while integrating local cultural relevance with a forward-looking market strategy.

"This grand opening in Shenzhen represents a meaningful step in our long-term vision to build Reborn Coffee into a global brand," said Jay Kim, Co-Chief Executive Officer of Reborn Coffee Inc. "We believe Shenzhen is one of the most strategically important cities in China, and we are proud to establish this flagship presence as a platform for continued growth across China and, over time, broader global market development."

items.t: Tencent's 2025 revenue beats estimates as Chinese tech giant ramps up AI investment
sum: Tencent on Wednesday reported full-year revenue that topped analyst predictions, as the Chinese tech giant continues to ramp up investments in AI.
- Revenue: 751.8 billion Chinese yuan ($109 billion), surpassing the 750.7 billion Chinese yuan expected by analysts, according to data compiled by LSEG.

"We sustained healthy growth rates in 2025, as AI capabilities improved our ad targeting and supported more engagement with our games, and as our cloud business delivered improving revenue growth and profit at scale," Ma Huateng, Chairman and CEO of Tencent, said in a statement.

"Our highly resilient and cash-generative core businesses provide us with the resources to fund our increasing investments in AI, including recruiting top-tier AI talent and upgrading our AI infrastructure."
Tencent spent 18 billion Chinese yuan on AI products in 2025 and plans to double that this year, the company said on a call with media.
The quarterly result was "solid" and broadly in line with Citi's expectations, analysts said in a note published shortly after the earnings statement.

A positive surprise came from accelerated business services revenue growth of 22% in the fourth quarter, supported by stronger cloud income across domestic and international markets — including AI-related services — as well as higher e-commerce technology fees, the Citi analysts said.

Tencent Jumps 6.2% as OpenClaw AI Frenzy Lifts Chinese Tech Shares
sum: China's rush to adopt the OpenClaw artificial intelligence agent is beginning to ripple through the country's technology sector, lifting several companies moving quickly to integrate the open-source software into their platforms. Tencent (TCEHY) climbed as much as 6.2% in Hong Kong trading after unveiling WorkBuddy, a workplace AI agent designed to run fully on OpenClaw, a move that investors appear to be interpreting as a signal that the company intends to play a larger role in the emerging AI-agent ecosystem.

The momentum around OpenClaw has been building since the tool launched in November, using large language models including Anthropic's Claude to handle routine digital tasks. Interest has accelerated globally this year, with the project surpassing Linux on GitHub's all-time star leaderboard in only a few months, while adoption in China appears particularly intense. Tencent recently began offering free installation of OpenClaw on its cloud platform, drawing long queues outside its headquarters according to local media, an early sign of the software's growing visibility.

Other Chinese AI developers are also moving rapidly to capture that demand. Knowledge Atlas Technology, known as Zhipu, jumped as much as 16% after introducing AutoClaw, a localized version of the software, while MiniMax advanced about 15% after releasing its own OpenClaw-based agent called MaxClaw. The broader enthusiasm has also extended to related cloud and software providers including UCloud Technology and QingCloud Technologies following earlier gains tied to government policies encouraging OpenClaw adoption, developments that some observers suggest could mark an important moment for China's fast-evolving AI landscape.

Tencent Considers Investing in Paramount’s $110 Billion Warner Bros. Deal
sum: Now that Netflix is out of the way, Tencent is considering investing several hundred million dollars in Paramount’s $110 billion deal for Warner Bros. Discovery, according to Bloomberg.

The Chinese tech giant previously committed $1 billion in equity financing for David Ellison’s bid, but later backed out to avoid raising potential national security concerns with U.S. regulators. The outlet noted that Tencent would be acting as a passive financial investor and may decide not to invest.
Representatives for Paramount and Tencent did not immediately return TheWrap’s request for comment.

Paramount will pay $31 per share in cash to acquire 100% of WBD’s total outstanding shares. The transaction is funded by $47 billion in equity, fully backed by the Ellison Family and RedBird Capital Partners, though it may include other strategic and financial partners at closing.

Tencent already holds a passive stake in Skydance. In addition to Tencent, three Middle Eastern sovereign wealth funds previously committed to provide a combined $24 billion in financing for Paramount’s previous WBD bids, which has prompted some lawmakers to call for a review by the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United Sates.

The deal also includes $54 billion of debt commitments from Bank of America, Citigroup, and Apollo, which includes $15 billion to backstop WBD’s existing bridge facility and $39 billion of incremental new debt. The $54 billion excludes $3.5 billion of bridge financing from these institutions to backstop an existing $3.5 billion revolving credit facility.

Existing Paramount stockholders will have the opportunity to participate in a rights offering of up to $3.25 billion of Class B Paramount stock alongside the new equity investment, which is expected to occur closer to the closing date, at a price of $16.02 per share.

items.t: Tencent halves stake in PB Fintech via Rs 695 Cr block deal
sum: Tencent Cloud Europe BV, an affiliate of Chinese internet giant Tencent, offloaded a portion of its stake in PB Fintech, the parent company of Policybazaar and Paisabazaar, through a block deal on Friday.
According to bulk deal data on the stock exchange, Tencent Cloud Europe BV sold 48,40,439 shares of PB Fintech at Rs 1,435.10 per share, taking the total transaction value to around Rs 694.65 crore.

Prior to the transaction, Tencent Cloud Europe held 97,48,750 shares, representing 2.12% stake in PB Fintech. Following the block deal, its holding reduced to 49,08,311 shares, or 1.06% in the company.

Several institutional investors participated in the block deal. DSP Mutual Fund acquired 3,25,643 shares worth Rs 46.73 crore, while Mirae Asset Mutual Fund purchased 9,00,000 shares valued at Rs 129.15 crore.

Meanwhile, Goldman Sachs entities were among the largest buyers in the transaction. Goldman Sachs Bank Europe SE bought 7,01,249 shares worth Rs 100.63 crore, while Goldman Sachs Bank Europe SE – ODI picked up 5,64,508 shares amounting to Rs 81 crore.
Other buyers included Schroder Asian Alpha Plus Fund, which purchased 3,46,958 shares worth Rs 49.8 crore, and Schroder AsiaPacific Fund PLC, which bought 2,57,081 shares valued at Rs 36.9 crore.

Société Générale (ODI) and Tata Mutual Fund acquired 7,00,000 shares (Rs 100.45 crore) and 3,45,000 shares (Rs 49.5 crore), respectively. Viridian Asia Opportunities Master Fund also bought 7,00,000 shares for Rs 100.45 crore.

sum: The gauge has fallen 5.5 per cent this year, while newly listed AI firms Zhipu AI, MiniMax and Beijing Haizhi are up at least fivefold
Hong Kong’s tech equity benchmark is struggling to balance the artificial intelligence frenzy and picking the right industry leaders, leading to its underperformance this year, according to analysts.

The Hang Seng Tech Index, which comprises 30 technology-related companies including Tencent Holdings, Alibaba Group Holding and Meituan, has fallen 5.5 per cent this year up to Friday, giving up some of last year’s 23.5 per cent gains.

In contrast, the broad-based Hang Seng Index has risen 0.3 per cent year to date. The city’s tech gauge has also been outpaced by the US’ tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 Index, which has fallen 0.8 per cent in the same period.

items.t: Speculation over higher gaming taxes hits Tencent shares, experts say unfounded
sum: Chinese internet stocks including Tencent Holdings fell sharply on Tuesday after online speculations suggested a tax increase on internet value-added services, though tax experts said the claims were unfounded. Tencent shares were briefly hit before trimming losses, as investors reacted to speculation that value-added tax (VAT) on internet services could be raised.

The speculations followed the implementation this year of China’s VAT Law and related regulations, after which the Ministry of Finance and the State Taxation Administration issued a series of supporting rules. Under the new measures, VAT on internet broadband access services provided by telecom operators such as China Mobile and China Unicom has been increased to 9% from 6%.

That change triggered speculation that major internet platforms, including Tencent, might face a similar tax increase. However, several senior tax experts said current VAT rules show no change to the 6% tax rate applied to internet companies’ core value-added services, dismissing the reports as rumours. Tencent, Other Chinese Tech Stocks Drop After VAT Hike Rumor
sum: (Yicai) Feb. 3 -- Chinese technology stocks retreated in Hong Kong, with Tencent Holdings among the biggest decliners, following speculation of an increase in value-added tax on internet firms. Tax experts said the rumor is unfounded and VAT rates are unchanged.

Tencent [HKG: 0700] closed 2.9 percent lower at HKD581 (USD74.36) per share today, recovering a little from a morning drop of as much as 6.3 percent. The Shenzhen-based firm’s stock has now fallen for more than four straight months.

Alibaba Group Holding [HKG: 9988] fell 1.4 percent to HKD161; Baidu [HKG: 9888] shed 3.6 percent to HKD141.40; Bilibili [HKG: 9626] gave up 2.5 percent to HKD253; and Kuaishou Technology [HKG: 1024] sank 4.6 percent to HKD73.45.

China’s new VAT Law came into effect on Jan. 1, aiming to clarify the tax and keeping key rates unchanged. The Ministry of Finance and the State Taxation Administration have since rolled out a series of supplementary rules, with the VAT rate for services including internet broadband access rising from 6 percent to 9 percent.
This triggered speculation that the rate applicable to the core businesses of internet companies, including Tencent, might also be raised.

But several senior tax experts told Yicai that Tencent’s core businesses mainly fall under the provision of value-added telecoms services and the sale of intangible assets, both of which are subject to a 6 percent tax rate.
According to currently disclosed VAT regulations, the rates remain at 6 percent, with no changes, the experts noted.

Best Stock to Buy Right Now: Alibaba vs. Tencent
sum: Alibaba (BABA -2.52%) and Tencent (TCEHY -0.88%) are two of China's largest tech companies. Alibaba owns the country's largest e-commerce marketplaces and top cloud infrastructure platform. Tencent owns China's largest social media platform, one of the country's leading cloud infrastructure platforms, and the world's largest video game publishing business. Both companies are expanding their artificial intelligence (AI) ecosystems with new large language models (LLMs), generative AI applications, and autonomous driving services.

Both stocks might appear to be reliable investments in China's economic expansion. Yet, over the past five years, Alibaba's stock has declined by nearly 40%, while Tencent's stock has risen by only 6%. They lost their luster as China's economic growth cooled off, they faced intense scrutiny from antitrust regulators, and the trade war curbed the market's appetite for Chinese equities. Should you invest in either of these out-of-favor Chinese bellwethers today?

Alibaba generates most of its revenue and profits from its two most significant Chinese marketplaces, Taobao and Tmall. A smaller slice of its revenue comes from its cloud infrastructure business, which operates at lower margins than its e-commerce marketplaces.

In 2021, China's antitrust regulators barred Taobao and Tmall from locking in their merchants with exclusive deals, using loss-leading promotions to gain new customers, and expanding with unapproved investments and acquisitions. Those restrictions throttled its growth and eroded its defenses against its top competitors, PDD (PDD -1.37%) and JD.com (JD -0.25%).

That pressure forced Alibaba to rely on its overseas marketplaces (including Lazada in Southeast Asia, Trendyol in Turkey, Daraz in South Asia, and AliExpress for cross-border purchases) and its Cainiao logistics business to drive its top-line growth. However, that strategy compresses its margins because those faster-growing businesses are still unprofitable.
From fiscal 2025 (which ended in March 2025) to fiscal 2028, analysts expect Alibaba's revenue and earnings per share (EPS) to grow at a CAGR of 8% and 11%, respectively.
